text: dsh-plugin-image-gen 为 DSH 提供图片生成工具，可通过用户配置的 OpenAI 兼容端点按提示生成图片，并将结果保存为 PNG 文件。它注册 generate_image 和 get_image_gen_config，支持模型、图片数量、尺寸、质量、输出目录和代理配置；配置诊断会展示端点与密钥解析状态，不显示密钥值。适合希望在 DSH 对话中生成并保存图片的用户。使用前需配置端点 API key。

dsh-plugin-image-gen adds image generation to DSH through a configurable OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Its tools create images from prompts, save PNG files, and report settings without revealing credentials. Configure models, image count, output directory, and an endpoint API key.
想在 DSH 对话里根据文字描述生成图片。
有没有工具能把生成的图片保存到本地目录？
让 DSH 通过我自己的 OpenAI 兼容图片接口画图。
我想一次生成几张不同版本的图片。
Generate an image from a prompt inside my DSH session.
Can DSH save images returned by my compatible image API?
dsh-plugin-image-gen 的功能「根据文字提示请求图片」：调用 generate_image 并传入 prompt；插件向配置的 OpenAI 兼容端点发送图片生成请求，可选模型、尺寸、质量和数量。
dsh-plugin-image-gen 的功能「将生成结果保存到文件」：端点返回 base64 图片或图片 URL 时，插件保存为 PNG，并在工具结果中给出绝对路径。
dsh-plugin-image-gen 的功能「查看生图配置诊断」：调用 get_image_gen_config 可查看有效端点、模型、配置文件位置和已解析密钥数量，不显示密钥值。
dsh-plugin-image-gen 的功能「配置端点与模型」：插件读取 image-gen.config.json，可指定 OpenAI 兼容 baseURL、模型列表、默认参数、超时、输出目录和代理。
想按提示词生成图片，并拿到保存文件的路径。
Use my configured image endpoint to create and save a few image variants.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · dsh-plugin-image-gen：Generate images from inside DeepSeek Harness (DSH) through **any OpenAI-compatible image endpoint you configure**. The package ships no endpoint, no model list tied to a vendor, and **no credentials** - you bring all three.

It registers two agent tools:

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · dsh-plugin-image-gen：| Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | generate_image | Generate image(s) from a prompt and save them to disk; returns absolute path(s). | | get_image_gen_config | Show the effective configuration and setup diagnostics (never secret values). |

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · What you need：- DSH (Desktop or CLI) with the tools service. Tested against DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2. - An image endpoint that speaks the OpenAI images API: POST {baseURL}/images/generations, returning data[].b64_json or data[].url. This covers OpenAI itself and most relays/gateways. - An API key for that endpoint. Nothing else: no system Node install, no dependencies, no build step.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Install：In DSH's **Plugins** page: - **Latest**: github:HaoyanZhang123/dsh-plugin-image-gen - **Pinned**: github:HaoyanZhang123/dsh-plugin-image-gen#v0.1.2 - **Offline**: download the .tgz from [Releases](https://github.com/HaoyanZhang123/dsh-plugin-image-gen/releases) and paste its absolute path - **npm** (if you prefer registry installs): dsh-plugin-image-gen

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Install：A fresh install takes effect immediately - the next turn already has both tools. **Upgrading** an already-installed version is the one case DSH reports as restart-required: quit and reopen DSH afterwards (closing the window is not quitting; use the tray icon).

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · 1. Find your DSH home：Everything lives there. Ask your agent to run get_image_gen_config - it prints the exact path in the "Config file" line. Or work it out: | Platform | Default DSH home | |---|---| | Windows | %USERPROFILE%\.dsh (for example C:\Users\you\.dsh) | | macOS / Linux | ~/.dsh | | Any, if set | whatever DSH_HOME points to |

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · 2. Add your API key：Pick whichever suits you: - In /.credentials.yaml, under the existing refs: section: ~~~yaml refs: IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY: your-api-key-here ~~~ - Or export IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY in the environment that launches DSH. - Or add IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY=your-api-key-here to /.env.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · 2. Add your API key：Resolution mirrors the official DSH layering: process environment > .credentials.yaml refs > /.env > /.env. Keys are **never** read from conversation, shown in tool output, or stored by this plugin. Do not paste your key into a chat message - put it in one of the three places above.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · 3. Point it at your endpoint：Create /image-gen.config.json: ~~~json { "baseURL": "https://your-relay.example.com/v1", "apiKeyEnv": "IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY", "models": ["gpt-image-1", "another-model"], "defaultModel": "gpt-image-1" } ~~~ That is the whole setup for most people. Skip this step entirely if you are using OpenAI itself with the default values - just add the key in step 2. Two practical notes:

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · 3. Point it at your endpoint：- baseURL is the part **before** /images/generations. If your gateway exposes images at https://gw.example.com/openai/v1/images/generations, set baseURL to https://gw.example.com/openai/v1. - On Windows, write paths in JSON with doubled backslashes ("E:\\images") or with forward slashes ("E:/images"). Edits take effect on the next tool call - no restart.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · 4. Verify：Ask your agent to run get_image_gen_config. You want to see your endpoint, your models, and Resolved keys: 1 (or more). Then say "generate an image of a red apple on a white table" and check the returned path on disk.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Using it：Just describe the image. Overrides are per call and phrased naturally: - "画一只在代码里游泳的猫" / "draw a cat swimming in code" - "a 16:9 banner for a launch post" - the agent passes a matching size - "four versions of the logo" - n=4 - "use another-model for this one" - a per-call model override

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Using it：Images are saved as PNG files and reported by absolute path, so they survive independently of the conversation. To view one in chat, the active model must accept image input - otherwise open the file.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Configuration reference：| Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | baseURL | https://api.openai.com/v1 | Any OpenAI-compatible base URL; POST /images/generations is called. | | apiKeyEnv | IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY | Credential name(s), comma-separated for rotation (for example KEY_A,KEY_B). Stores names, never keys. | | models | ["gpt-image-1"] | Model ids shown to the agent; it may pass any id. | | defaultModel | first of models | Used when a call does not specify model. | | defaultParams | {} | Extra request fields merged into every call - the escape hatch for provider-specific parameters such as aspect_ratio or style. | | timeoutMs | 240000 | Per-request timeout. | | outputDir | /image-gen/output | Where images are saved; per-call output_dir overrides. | | proxy | auto | auto (keep an environment proxy, else detect the OS system proxy: Windows regist

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Configuration reference：Layering: package defaults < the entry's optional config: block in the profile patch < image-gen.config.json. size and quality are **pass-through strings**: they are sent only when you set them (per call or via defaultParams); otherwise the endpoint applies its own defaults. Vocabulary differs per provider - the plugin never validates them, and endpoint errors are returned verbatim so the agent can retry.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Cause and fix | |---|---| | No API key found for "IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY" | Step 2 was skipped, or the key sits under a name that differs from apiKeyEnv. Run get_image_gen_config to see which names are consulted. | | Configuration warnings: ... invalid JSON | The config file failed to parse and was ignored; defaults apply. Validate the JSON and check for Windows backslashes. | | upstream HTTP 401 | The endpoint rejected the key (wrong key, wrong account, or a key for a different gateway). | | upstream HTTP 404 | baseURL is wrong - usually it already includes or omits /v1. The called URL is {baseURL}/images/generations. | | upstream HTTP 429 | Rate limited. Add a second key to apiKeyEnv (KEY_A,KEY_B); the plugin rotates on 401/429. | | upstream returned no image data | The endpoint answered, but not in OpenAI image shape (data[].b64_json / data[].url). It is not compatible. | | Request timed out | Raise timeoutMs. Large sizes
dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Troubleshooting：Anything else: the error text is returned verbatim from the endpoint, and get_image_gen_config reports the effective settings and config-file path.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Security：- The published package contains no endpoint beyond the neutral OpenAI default and no credentials; the files whitelist in package.json defines exactly what ships. - npm run pack:check packs the tarball and scans every shipped file for key-shaped strings before a release. - API keys resolve only from your own credential stores and never appear in logs, tool output, or errors.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Compatibility and failure behavior：See [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md). In short: the plugin imports only Node builtins and the documented tool-registration contract, declares **no DSH version gate at all**, and fails loudly and locally if that contract ever changes. It is tested against DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 on Windows; macOS uses the same contracts (system-proxy detection covered by unit tests).
dsh-plugin-image-gen README · Uninstall：Remove the bundle in the Plugins page. Your image-gen.config.json, saved images, and credentials are left untouched.

dsh-plugin-image-gen README · For maintainers：~~~bash node --test # 37 tests node tools/check-package.mjs # file whitelist + credential-leak scan, then packs the tarball ~~~ Release flow: bump version in package.json, add a CHANGELOG entry, run both commands, commit, then gh release create vX.Y.Z dsh-plugin-image-gen-X.Y.Z.tgz.
